newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says metal dispute in home straight.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says metal dispute in home straight.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Sunday that a bitter and protracted metalworkers' dispute over pay was now entering the home straight and he expected a deal to be signed soon.
"Tomorrow is the start of the last round," Prodi told reporters in the northern city of Bologna. "I think all the elements are in place to get ready to sign."
Italy's three main trades union confederations, CGIL, CISL and UIL, are due to meet the employers' umbrella group Confindustria for talks on Monday.
The dispute, which affects some 1.7 million workers in a sector accounting for 40 percent of Italian industrial output, is expected to set the tone for pay deals in other sectors.
Metalworkers unions have already staged a series of strikes to press their claims for increases in wage contracts for the 1996-98 period. The previous contracts ran out in June.

The government suggested in December that management should raise pay by an average 200,000 lire ($125) a month. Union leaders, who had sought a 230,000 lire rise, accepted but the main industry group Federmeccanica rejected it as inflationary.

The dispute centres on the interpretation of a landmark wage 1993 deal between the labour confederations, Confindustria and the government, which scrapped automatic index-linked pay rises. Federmeccanica has stuck to its original 139,000 lire offer.
"The government has done its bit, but we can't take the place of Federmeccanica, of Confindustria and of union organisations," Prodi said.
"We have been in constant contact with all sides and have worked hard to prepare a solution and I believe that now all the elements are in place for a deal to be signed."
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Saturday that the government was "putting a lot of faith" in Monday's meeting. ($1=1,588 lire)
